summary: The narrator meets Barry Morton, an official in Guatemala, who is evasive about a foreigner's foul play and says local officials prefer not to dig too deeply into such cases. The narrator then notices a silver cat pendant on Morton's secretary, a stout Ladino woman, which resembles jewelry he remembers from Kevin and Rachel, and wonders whether she knows more than her boss. The passage ends with the narrator turning his thoughts to Steve, whom he has not seen in three and a half months. A stray unrelated sentence about the Garden of Earthly Delights painting appears in the middle of the text.
one_line: A narrator presses evasive official Barry Morton in Guatemala about a foreigner's foul play and notices a cat pendant worn by his secretary.
key_facts: The narrator says that Barry Morton knows more than he is telling him.
Barry Morton handles an ornate letter opener with an onyx jaguar head on its handle.
Morton says the sovereign state of Guatemala definitely plays by its own rules.
Morton says lower-level officials have developed a consensus that sometimes it's better not to be too industrious when foreigners meet with foul play.
The narrator suspects that official dom in Guatemala may have had something to do with what happened to the woman.
The secretary is described as a stout, fiftyish Ladino matron with defiantly black-dyed hair.
The secretary wears a small silver pendant shaped like the face of a cat, most likely the local jaguar.
The narrator recalls seeing similar pendants with Kevin and Rachel.
The back of the secretary's medallion is blank silver, with no engraving of lines and dots.
The narrator decides not to ask the secretary about the pendant, expecting more BS runaround.
The narrator wonders whether the secretary handles matters that never reach Barry Morton's desk.
The narrator has not seen Steve in three and a half months and wants to recapture the lost time.
The text includes an unrelated sentence that in 2013 Mandy finally saw the original Garden of Earthly Delights painting up close after waiting in line for hours.
